destination.name: Goolwa
destination.tagline: A river-port town where the Murray meets the sea, with a barrage and a wharf precinct.
destination.description: Goolwa sits on the lower Murray where the river meets Lake Alexandrina, a few kilometres from the Southern Ocean. A series of barrages holds back the sea, and you can walk halfway across the Goolwa Barrage. The wharf precinct has an interpretive centre on the Murray Mouth, and a bridge leads to Hindmarsh Island and its waterbirds. A surf beach runs south-east of town, and Strathalbyn and Langhorne Creek are an easy drive inland.
whyVisit: Walk out across the Murray barrage
Watch waterbirds near the Murray Mouth

goodToKnow.title: Barrage access is from Goolwa
goodToKnow.detail: Reach the barrage by Barrage Road from the Goolwa side. There is no way onto it from Hindmarsh Island.

goodToKnow.title: Check beach driving rules
goodToKnow.detail: Four-wheel drives use the track behind the surf club, best at low tide with tyres lowered. Rules change, so check with the council.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Visit in {months} for mild days on the river and beach. Summer is hotter and winter is wetter.
